name: いきいき亭 近江町店 (Ikiikitei Omicho-ten)

claims.text: A roughly 10-seat market counter doing sushi and raw-fish bowls, with shared prep surfaces and no documented allergen separation.
Seafood bowls and nigiri are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which is brewed with wheat; sushi rice is also vinegar-seasoned.
The whole menu is fish-based (Kanazawa Port seafood bowls and sushi), with no vegan or vegetarian dishes offered.
Menu centers on seafood rice bowls and tempura bowls; wheat-based soy sauce and fish dashi are used throughout, and there is no gluten-free menu or accommodation.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (which contains wheat) is used to season the seafood bowls; no wheat-free tamari is mentioned.
Every dish is built on raw fish, seafood and fish-based dashi; there are no documented vegan options.

name: 石臼挽き手打ちそば 村田屋 (Ishiusubiki Teuchi Soba Murataya)

claims.text: The soba noodles are made as 外一 (about 80% buckwheat, 20% wheat flour), so the noodles themselves contain wheat — not safe for celiac or gluten-free diners.
Soba is served with a traditional dashi-and-soy tsuyu/dipping sauce, which is wheat-containing and fish-based; no wheat-free sauce is documented.
Broth is bonito/kombu dashi-based and signature dishes use duck and tempura, so animal products are central; no vegan preparation is documented.
Menu relies on soy sauce, miso, and dashi with fried items (tempura, fried white shrimp) sharing the kitchen; no gluten-free accommodation is documented.
Sashimi and izakaya dishes are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.
Seafood and dashi are central to nearly every dish; vegetable preparations are typically dashi-based.

name: 自家焙煎 東出珈琲店 (Jikabaisen Higashide Coffee Ten)

claims.text: Homemade desserts contain eggs, fresh cream, milk and vanilla beans, and milk drinks are dairy-based; no dairy-free or vegan options are documented.
Black self-roasted coffee is naturally plant-based and gluten-free, and the menu is simple (coffee plus a couple of homemade desserts), making it easy to order a plain black coffee.

name: かばやきの浅田 (Kabayaki no Asada)

claims.text: The signature tare is built on premium soy sauce, sugar, mirin and sake; Japanese soy sauce and mirin typically contain wheat, so the glaze is a gluten source.
The shop sells only grilled loach (a freshwater fish); there are no plant-based items, so it is unsuitable for vegans.
Okonomiyaki batter, yakisoba noodles, takoyaki and taiyaki are all wheat-flour based and prepared on a shared teppan griddle, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with okonomiyaki/yakisoba sauce, which is typically wheat-based; no gluten-free sauce is documented.
Egg batter, seafood (Noto oysters, octopus), dashi and beef-tendon stew are core to the menu and share the same griddle, so plant-based dishes cannot be reliably separated.

name: 加登長 総本店 (Kadocho Sohonten)

claims.text: A wheat-noodle kitchen serving udon, soba, tempura and tonkatsu; flour and wheat-based broth are pervasive, making cross-contamination unavoidable for gluten-sensitive diners.
The broth combines Kansai dashi with Kanazawa sweet soy sauce; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Base broth is a fish dashi (urume sardine, mackerel, bonito), so even vegetable dishes are prepared in an animal-stock kitchen.
